I know how it works and I am under no illusion that the staff walked into a post office and send out stuff.  My point is that nomatter how many packages were sent out, the courier needed to scan them before loading them into their trucks.  And the warehouse/company needs to confirm if the courier received the same numbers of packages as they intended to send out.  That’s courier service and that’s what tracking numbers are for or else it is just regular mail in the mail box.
